title: GDR-learners: Orthogonal Learning of Generative Models for Potential Outcomes
claim: Summarizing outcomes by their mean hides uncertainty; modeling the full outcome distribution reveals heavy tails and multi-modality that decisions need.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right, shared axes, dotted slices on right
description: Two side-by-side line-plot panels share the same axes: patient characteristic x on the horizontal axis and potential outcome y on the vertical axis. The left panel, titled CAPO, shows two smooth curves. An orange curve for treatment Y[1] rises and plateaus. A blue curve for control Y[0] stays low and flat. Rounded boxes on the right label them E(Y[1]|x) and E(Y[0]|x). The right panel, titled CDPO, uses the same two thin mean curves. It adds vertical dotted lines at evenly spaced x values, and each line carries a sideways orange or blue density curve. The densities are skewed, wide, and bimodal in places. Boxes label them P(Y[1]|x) and P(Y[0]|x). Orange and blue encode treated and control groups throughout. The eye goes first to the contrast between the clean left curves and the dense right densities.
caption: Capturing the uncertainty in POs helps make reliable treatment decisions. Unlike conditional average potential outcomes (CAPOs, left), conditional distributions of potential outcomes (CDPOs, right) allow for quantifying the aleatoric uncertainty of the POs. As a result, they capture more information about the potential outcomes, such as heavy tails or multi-modalities.
abstract: Various deep generative models have been proposed to estimate potential outcomes distributions from observational data. However, none of them have the favorable theoretical property of general Neyman-orthogonality and, associated with it, quasi-oracle efficiency and double robustness. In this paper, we introduce a general suite of generative Neyman-orthogonal (doubly-robust) learners that estimate the conditional distributions of potential outcomes. Our proposed generative doubly-robust learners (GDR-learners) are flexible and can be instantiated with many state-of-the-art deep generative models. In particular, we develop GDR-learners based on (a) conditional normalizing flows (which we call GDR-CNFs), (b) conditional generative adversarial networks (GDR-CGANs), (c) conditional variational autoencoders (GDR-CVAEs), and (d) conditional diffusion models (GDR-CDMs). Unlike the existing methods, our GDR-learners possess the properties of quasi-oracle efficiency and rate double robustness, and are thus asymptotically optimal. In a series of (semi-)synthetic experiments, we demonstrate that our GDR-learners are very effective and outperform the existing methods in estimating the conditional distributions of potential outcomes.
